# Project Parva LLM Context

Project Parva is an open-source proof-carrying temporal infrastructure project
for Nepali date and time systems. It is broader than a calendar API: it
combines deterministic APIs, source/method dockets, policy traces, field
provenance, boundary vectors, proof receipts, replay verification, local/offline
fixtures, SDKs, AI-safe tools, and public verification gates.

## Core Capabilities

- BS to AD conversion
- AD to BS conversion
- BS date validation
- holiday membership and non-membership checks
- working-day decision support
- fiscal-year metadata
- BS month metadata with canonical, solar-civil, static-lookup, and compare modes
- method-docketed Panchanga summary
- payroll/date-risk audit prechecks
- local/offline proof verification

## Proof Mode

Several routes support `proof=compact`, `proof=audit`, `proof=replay`, or
`proof=membrane`. Proof responses include:

- capsule
- identity hash
- witness hash
- result
- field provenance
- boundary vector
- source or method docket references
- policy decision trace
- proof pack

Proof verifiers must replay operation semantics or validate pinned fixture
content. A verifier that only checks object shape or hash presence is not
sufficient.

## Panchanga

Panchanga output is computed and method-backed. It discloses location, timezone,
ephemeris provider, provider kind, fixture or kernel hash where applicable,
ayanamsa, sunrise rule, method dockets, field provenance, and non-authority
boundaries. JPL support is an explicit provider interface and configuration path;
large kernels are not bundled.

## Agent Behavior

Agents should call Parva tools or APIs instead of guessing Nepali dates. Agents
must preserve `review_required`, `not_authority`, source/method status, and
proof links. Agents must not present Parva as final authority for official,
legal, tax, payroll, banking, religious, ritual, or unsupported future-date
decisions.

## Forbidden Claims

Do not claim government authority, legal authority, tax authority, payroll
authority, banking authority, religious authority, official future date
authority, official Panchanga authority, external certification, package
publication, registry acceptance, customers, adoption, or public exact
unsupported Future-BS predictions unless the repository contains real evidence.
